P projects to a single transverse coordinate. Therefore the section of P+B at y+y_P is exactly P+B_y. Brunn–Minkowski in the common r-plane gives the strict factor 2^r on each positive-volume section, including intervals when r=1.

Fubini gives strict global growth since the set of positive-volume sections contributes b>0. At r=d the whole-space comparison applies directly. Every omitted normal strictly misses the single midpoint set because P is strictly below −1 and B is at or below 1.
The midpoint volume scales by 2^(−d), giving b/2^(d−k+1). For k=m the entire T is an r-section and |P|>|T|, so |A|>|T|≥b. Compared with 5dd69a77cceb0773 §§1 and 4.
